items.title: Overview of the 2025 FDA circulatory systems devices panel advisory committee meeting on the V-Wave Ventura Interatrial Shunt System.
items.abstract: Interatrial shunting is a novel strategy to reduce left atrial pressure and heart-failure (HF) morbidity. The Ventura Interatrial Shunt System (V-Wave) was evaluated in the randomized, sham-controlled RELIEVE-HF trial and reviewed by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) Circulatory Systems Devices Panel. To summarize the scientific and regulatory deliberations among the sponsor, FDA, and Advisory Panel regarding the safety, effectiveness, and benefit-risk profile V-Wave. We reviewed publicly available FDA documents, sponsor presentations, FDA analyses, and Advisory Panel discussions from the December 2025 meeting, with emphasis on trial design, endpoint selection, subgroup interpretation, and regulatory standards. The sponsor emphasized reductions in recurrent HF events among patients with HF with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF), supported by prespecified recurrent-event analyses and echocardiographic data, while arguing that the hierarchical win-ratio primary endpoint underestimated benefits. In contrast, the FDA highlighted the failure to meet the prespecified primary endpoint in the intention-to-treat population, the fragility of subgroup findings, lack of outcome improvement, and consistent harm in patients with preserved ejection fraction. Advisory Panel members acknowledged acceptable procedural safety but expressed concern regarding the absence of clear, reproducible efficacy, challenges in phenotype-based labeling, and the inability of post-approval registries to resolve evidence gaps. The Advisory Panel unanimously concluded that, despite procedural safety, the evidence did not demonstrate a favorable benefit-risk profile for the V-Wave device. The deliberations underscore the challenges of relying on subgroup analyses, recurrent-event endpoints, and post-market data to support approval of permanent intracardiac devices in this population.

items.title: Supradiaphragmatic Epicardial Pacemaker Implantation for Pseudoatrioventricular Block in Neonatal Long QT Syndrome: Genotype-agnostic Anesthetic Strategy Pending Genetic Diagnosis.
items.abstract: A late-preterm female neonate (35+3 weeks gestation) was delivered via emergency cesarean section due to fetal bradycardia. Electrocardiography revealed a 2:1 pseudoatrioventricular block, a wide QRS complex, and a corrected QT interval of 495 ms, a pattern typically associated with long QT syndrome type 2 (KCNH2) or type 3 (SCN5A). Additional findings included a large patent ductus arteriosus, moderate apical muscular ventricular septal defect, glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase deficiency, neonatal hypoglycemia, and hyperbilirubinemia. Following preoperative QT stabilization with intravenous magnesium sulfate, the infant underwent epicardial single-chamber permanent pacemaker implantation (VVI 120 bpm) via lower partial sternotomy, with a supradiaphragmatic pericardial generator pocket, on day of life (DOL) 4, at an operative weight of 2.37 kg. Anesthesia was administered using a genotype-agnostic total intravenous anesthesia strategy, comprising propofol and remifentanil with cisatracurium neuromuscular blockade, while avoiding volatile and QT-prolonging agents, optimizing electrolytes, and maintaining external defibrillator readiness. This approach was designed to be safe irrespective of the underlying channelopathy. No intraoperative arrhythmia was observed. Postoperative genetic testing unexpectedly identified a heterozygous KCNQ1 variant c.1273C>A p.(Leu425Met), confirming LQT1 (a potassium channelopathy), contradicting the preoperative electrocardiography-based assumption of sodium channelopathy. Device interrogation on DOL 14 confirmed satisfactory parameters, and the infant was discharged on propranolol on DOL 15 without further arrhythmic events. This case demonstrates that 2:1 pseudoatrioventricular block, typically associated with LQT2/LQT3, can manifest in LQT1, and that a genotype-agnostic total intravenous anesthesia strategy is an appropriate anesthetic approach when the genetic subtype is unknown prior to urgent neonatal long QT syndrome surgery.

[ 18 F]fluorodeoxyglucose-PET in Therapeutic Decision-Making and Theranostics of Breast Cancer.
items.abstract: [ 18 F]fluorodeoxyglucose (FDG)-PET/CT informs decisions at almost every point in breast cancer care. It establishes the extent of disease at diagnosis and so determines whether treatment is delivered with curative or palliative intent. This review examines the biology that underlies FDG uptake and explains why uptake varies so markedly between molecular subtypes. It also sets out the evidence supporting FDG-PET/CT in staging and in therapeutic decision-making across chemotherapy, endocrine therapy, HER2-directed treatment, immunotherapy, and radiotherapy planning, before turning to the complimentary role of 18F-FDG PET/CT with theranostic agents.

items.title: [The role of endothelial cells in regulating T cell infiltration and activation in tumor progression and immunotherapy].
items.abstract: Endothelial cell (EC) serves as the fundamental structural and functional units of the vascular system, playing pivotal roles in maintaining tissue homeostasis and regulating immune responses. Recent studies have shown that EC dynamically regulates T cell chemotaxis, infiltration, and activation through surface molecules (e.g., adhesion and co-stimulating/inhibitory molecules), paracrine factors (chemokines, metabolites), and exosomes. These mechanisms are crucial in shaping the tumor immune microenvironment. In the tumor microenvironment (TME), EC dysfunction impairs T cell recruitment and promotes immunosuppression, leading to a "cold tumor" phenotype and immunotherapy resistance. Targeting key pathways such as vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF), cyclic GMP-AMP synthase-stimulator of interferon genes (cGAS-STING), and lymphotoxin beta receptor (LTβR) via anti-angiogenic therapy can reverse EC dysfunction, normalize blood vessels, and enhance T cell-mediated antitumor immunity. This review systematically summarizes the molecular mechanisms by which EC regulate T cell infiltration and activation during tumor progression and immunotherapy, providing new theoretical insights and strategic perspectives for combining anti-angiogenic therapy with immunotherapy.

Next-generation dendritic cell and exosome vaccines in NSCLC: integrating personalized medicine, nanotechnology, AI, and microfluidics for enhanced immunotherapy.
items.abstract: Lung cancer remains the leading cause of cancer-related mortality, and non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) accounts for most cases. Despite advances in immune checkpoint inhibition, many patients do not respond, prompting interest in Dendritic Cell (DC) vaccines and DC-derived Exosome (DEX) platforms as personalized immunotherapeutic strategies. This narrative review examines the current clinical status of DC and DEX vaccines in NSCLC. It distinguishes therapeutic DEX products from tumor-derived extracellular vesicles, circulating diagnostic biomarkers, and exosome-mimetic nanoparticles, which differ in source, function, production, and regulation. PubMed, Google Scholar, and ClinicalTrials.gov were searched from 2000 to 2026; no formal risk-of-bias assessment or dual screening was performed, and selection bias cannot be excluded. No head-to-head clinical comparison of DCVs and DEX vaccines exists in NSCLC, and neither is supported by phase III data. We assess four enabling technologies, microfluidics, AI, nanoparticle engineering, and personalized medicine, and identify unresolved obstacles, including absent validated predictive biomarkers, lack of DEX-specific Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) and potency standards, inter-batch variability, regulatory ambiguity, high costs, and biological heterogeneity, before proposing an explicitly hypothetical closed-loop approach. Clinical translation requires standardized methodology, validated biomarkers, GMP-compliant production, prospective trials in earlier-stage disease, and direct comparison of DCV and DEX platforms. Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer (NSCLC) is the most prevalent kind of lung cancer, which continues to be the primary cause of cancer-related deaths globally. Many patients do not respond to immunotherapies, even though others do. Dendritic Cells (DCs), specialized immune cells that help the body identify and fight cancer, are a viable platform for developing customized vaccines. However, they have drawbacks, including high cost and complex production. An alternative strategy uses exosomes, microscopic particles DCs release that carry crucial immune signals. Exosomes can activate the immune system in several ways and are safer than whole cells, though more research is needed to confirm their effectiveness. Artificial intelligence can help create customized vaccines based on each patient’s tumor; nanoparticles can deliver vaccines more precisely to target cells; microfluidic devices can quickly separate and engineer exosomes; and nanotheranostics may enable real-time monitoring of treatment responses. Although encouraging, most of these methods are still in their infancy and have been tested only in cells or animals, not in humans. We conclude that these vaccines are not yet ready for widespread use and that the next step is carefully planned clinical trials with specific objectives. We should not make more promises than the facts warrant.

items.title: CRISPR, mRNA, and Beyond: Nucleic Acid Therapeutics in Allergy and Immunology.
items.abstract: The management of allergic and immunologic diseases has long centered on symptom management rather than disease modification. Conventional pharmacotherapy controls manifestations of the immune dysregulation but does little to treat the underlying cause. Newer monoclonal and small molecule therapies target downstream effectors of the type 2 inflammatory cascade, and allergen immunotherapy, while disease-modifying, requires years of administration for effect. Nucleic acid therapies represent a different approach that intervenes at the level of genetic information itself, at the DNA, RNA, or protein-production step. This includes mRNA treatments that direct cells to produce therapeutic proteins or modify allergen-specific immune responses; antisense oligonucleotides and small interfering RNAs that selectively silence disease genes; adeno-associated viral vectors for sustained gene delivery; and CRISPR-based systems that permanently edit the genome. Several technologies have advanced to clinical proof of concept including a CRISPR gene-editing therapy (lonvoguran ziclumeran) that reduced hereditary angioedema attacks by 87% compared with placebo in a randomized controlled trial. An inhaled DNAzyme targeting the intracellular transcription factor GATA3 attenuated allergen-induced late asthmatic responses by 34% in humans, and CD19 CAR-T cell therapy induced drug-free remission in severe autoimmune disease. As of 2025, 24 oligonucleotide therapeutics have received FDA approval, including donidalorsen, the first RNA-targeted prophylactic therapy approved for hereditary angioedema. This review examines each therapeutic technology, its mechanism and delivery strategy, and the evidence relevant to allergic and immunologic disease. Persistent challenges, including delivery beyond the liver, immune responses to viral vectors, and the need for long-term safety data, are addressed alongside a proposed integration with existing treatment paradigms.

items.title: β-Amyrin,an active compound of Bryophyllum pinnatum,alleviates alcoholic liver disease by regulating AKT1 expression and enhancing antioxidant defense.
items.abstract: Bryophyllum pinnatum (L. f.) Oken (BP), a traditional hepatoprotective herb, has demonstrated therapeutic potential in managing liver disorders. However, the specific bioactive compounds of BP and its mechanisms against alcoholic liver disease (ALD) remain unclear. In this study, the bioactive compounds of BP were screened by database mining and their targets were predicted. A compound-target-disease network was constructed to identify core targets, followed by molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulation to validate the binding of β-Amyrin with AKT1. The hepatoprotective efficacy and mechanism were finally verified in ethanol-exposed HepG2 cells. A database screening process has identified four bioactive compounds (β-Amyrin, Astragalin, α-Amyrin and Bryophyllin A). Network pharmacology analyses revealed 138 common targets, primarily associated with lipid metabolism, hepatitis B and C, and the PI3K/AKT signaling pathway, and core targets included AKT1, CCND1, EGFR, HIF1A and SRC. Notably, in vitro experiments using ethanol-exposed HepG2 cells demonstrated that β-Amyrin significantly reduced transaminase (ALT, AST), total cholesterol (TC) and triglyceride (TG). Additionally, β-Amyrin enhanced antioxidant defense (SOD, CAT, GSH) and suppressed malondialdehyde (MDA) accumulation. Furthermore, β-Amyrin alleviated intracellular lipid accumulation as evidenced by Oil Red O staining. Mechanistically, β-Amyrin restored the expression of total AKT1 and its phosphorylation level (p-AKT1), which could be abolished by AKT1-specific inhibitor MK2206. This is the first study to identify β-Amyrin as the key bioactive compound of BP against ALD, and these findings provide compelling evidence for BP's potential as a therapeutic strategy for ALD.

items.title: MiR-223 and miR-323 as biomarkers of inflammatory and neuropsychiatric alterations in long COVID with chronic viral hepatitis.
items.abstract: Long COVID involves persistent physical, mental, and functional symptoms following SARS-CoV-2 infection. Its biological mechanisms remain poorly understood, particularly with chronic viral hepatitis. This study investigated associations between microRNA (miRNA) expression and mental and physical health outcomes in individuals with Long COVID, considering chronic hepatitis B or C. This cross-sectional study included 80 individuals divided into four groups (n = 20 each): Long COVID, chronic viral hepatitis, Long COVID with hepatitis, and controls. Depression, anxiety, quality of life, fatigue, and functional status were assessed using validated scales, including the Post-COVID Functional Status Scale. Expression of miR-122, miR-143, miR-223, and miR-323 was quantified by RT-qPCR. Associations were evaluated using non-parametric tests and correlation analyses. MiR-143, miR-223, and miR-323 were significantly upregulated in individuals with Long COVID and hepatitis. MiRNA expression was associated with mental and physical health outcomes, particularly through a positive correlation between miR-323 expression and anxiety levels in individuals with Long COVID and hepatitis. MiR-223 was the only miRNA significantly overexpressed in this group compared with all other groups, suggesting its potential as a biomarker of coexisting conditions. Depression and anxiety affected up to 75% and 50% of individuals in the Long COVID groups, respectively (p < 0.05).These findings suggest that circulating miRNAs, particularly miR-223, miR-143, and miR-323, are associated with Long COVID in the presence of chronic viral hepatitis and may serve as biomarkers of disease burden and clinical heterogeneity.

items.title: Prevalence and outcomes of co-occurring mental/physical comorbidities and substance use disorders: An atlas umbrella review including 156 systematic reviews with meta-analysis.
items.abstract: Substance use disorders(SUDs) are intertwined with psychiatric and general medical disorders. Substances of abuse also exert intrinsic toxicities and adverse effects that contribute to extensive somatic multimorbidity, complicating patient prognoses. This umbrella review(UR) systematically aggregated, harmonized, and graded the credibility of meta-analytic evidence concerning SUD comorbidities across psychiatric/somatic dimensions. We searched major electronic databases up to July 2026 for systematic reviews with meta-analyses of observational studies mapping SUD co-occurrences. Extracted data were categorized by ICD-11 diagnostic blocks. Meta-analytic estimates were evaluated using pre-registered quantitative credibility indicators assessing sample size(N), number of studies(k), 95%confidence interval(95%CI) widths, and heterogeneity(I 2 ). The review included 156 systematic reviews with meta-analysis, encompassing 100,441,167 database/registry records across 14,322 study entries, with possible overlap across reviews. High-credibility data showed a strong intra-block psychiatric overlap: Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder demonstrated a pooled SUD prevalence of 21.0%(95%CI=17.0-25.0%;k = 31), while Major Depressive Disorder reached a prevalence of 36.1%(95%CI=32.4%-39.7%;k = 161) among patients with Opioid Use Disorder(OUD). Somatic toxicities and iatrogenic pathways were highly prevalent: opioid analgesic use in chronic noncancer pain 27.0%(95%C.I.=23.0-31.0%;N > 3.9 M), and in post-lumbar fusion surgery patients (40.0%;95%C.I.=32.0-49.0%). High prevalences of syndemic infectious comorbidities were observed among populations with injection drug use, with Hepatitis C virus prevalence reaching 61.0%(95%CI=56.0-67.0%) in regional cohorts. Highly specific associations revealed that schizotypal traits strongly correlate with Cannabis Use Disorder(I 2 =0%). SUDs are multi-systemic disorders characterized by substantial cross-block psychiatric/medical multimorbidity. The breadth and the credibility gradient of multimorbidity argue for routine cross-domain screening and coordinated care, with model effectiveness left to trials.

items.title: Prevalence of anti-HCV and incidence rate of HCV seroconversion in a large multiregional health check-up population in China: a cross-sectional and longitudinal study of 1.6 million adults.
items.abstract: China carries one of the heaviest burdens of hepatitis C virus (HCV) infection worldwide. This study aimed to estimate the prevalence of anti-HCV and incidence rate of HCV seroconversion in a large health check-up population in China. This cross-sectional, and longitudinal study used data from the Meinian health check-up database, covering participants from all 31 provinces of mainland China between 2017 and 2023. Serological samples were tested for anti-HCV using ELISA. The weighted prevalence of anti-HCV and the incidence rate of HCV seroconversion were calculated. Poisson regression was used to identify risk factors for HCV seroconversion. A total of 1,610,735 participants were included in the analysis of anti-HCV prevalence. The prevalence of anti-HCV in the study population was 0.89% (95% CI, 0.77%-1.01%), with significantly higher prevalence found in females and elderly individuals. Geographically, the prevalence was significantly higher in Central and West China compared to East China. Individuals with abnormal liver function or liver fibrosis, abnormal thyroid function or antibodies, diabetes, and impaired kidney function had significantly higher prevalence. The analysis of HCV seroconversion included 179,447 participants, showing an incidence rate of 0.72 per 1,000 person-years during a median follow-up of 1.5 years. Risk factors for HCV seroconversion included older age, as well as living in Central or West China, border regions, areas with low GDP per capita, and areas with high anti-HCV prevalence. Our study reveals significant anti-HCV seroprevalence burden and ongoing risk of HCV transmission in a large health check-up population in China, highlighting the urgent need for systematic screening and enhanced prevention efforts to control HCV transmission.

items.title: A Multichannel and Multimodal Combined Model Based on 2.5D Deep Learning For Predicting Tumor-Free Survival After Liver Transplantation In Hepatocellular Carcinoma: A 7-Year Retrospective Study.
items.abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) accounts for 90% of primary liver cancers and ranks as the fourth leading cause of cancer-related deaths worldwide. This study aimed to promptly identify high-risk patients for early recurrence after liver transplantation (LT), thereby optimizing personalized follow-up and intervention strategies for patients with HCC. A retrospective cohort of 143 patients with HCC was selected. Following the collection of imaging investigations, clinical data, and postoperative follow-up information, we developed a combined model based on 2.5-dimensional (2.5D) deep learning (DL). This model integrates clinical features, radiomics characteristics, and DL data across multiple modalities, utilizing multichannel 2.5D data comprising coronal, sagittal, and peritumoral slices of the largest tumor area. Model performance was assessed through receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves, calibration curves, and decision curve analysis (DCA). The 2.5D DL model demonstrated superior performance over the 2D DL model, achieving area under the ROC curve (AUC) values of 0.784/0.842, 0.799/0.843, and 0.824/0.827 in the training and testing cohorts, compared to the 2D model's 0.736/0.819, 0.751/0.818, and 0.724/0.803. The combined model significantly surpassed other models, attaining C-index values of 0.789/0.826 in the training and testing cohorts, along with 1-year, 2-year, and 3-year AUC values of 0.842/0.931, 0.865/0.891, and 0.853/0.885, respectively. Furthermore, the combined model demonstrated the highest consistency in calibration curves and provided the greatest clinical net benefit in DCA. The combined model based on 2.5D DL demonstrates robust applicability and high predictive performance in identifying early postoperative recurrence of HCC. This strategy facilitates proactive and individualized intervention for high-risk patients, thereby improving clinical outcomes.

items.title: Elevated Risk of Bladder Cancer Associated With Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Steatotic Liver Disease in Elderly Korean Men: A Nationwide Cohort Study.
items.abstract: Steatotic liver disease (SLD) is one of the major metabolic disorders associated with various extrahepatic malignancies. Although growing evidence suggests a link between SLD and bladder cancer, the precise nature of this relationship remains unclear. The goal of our study was to explore the relationship between SLD subtypes and the risk of bladder cancer in elderly Korean men. This nationwide population-based cohort study utilized data from South Korean men aged 65 years and older, collected from 2009 to 2010. The subdistribution hazard ratios (SHRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were evaluated using the Fine and Gray regression model, with all-cause mortality considered as a competing event. Inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW) was applied to the SLD and non-SLD groups to create a pseudo-population, enabling a more unbiased evaluation. Overall, the bladder cancer incidence was compared across the SLD and non-SLD groups. Among 89,903 Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Steatotic Liver Disease (MASLD) participants, 1,048 bladder cancer cases were identified, compared to 935 in 84,111 non-SLD participants after IPTW (1.17% vs. 1.11%). In MASLD with increased alcohol intake (MetALD) group, 456 cases were found among 61,709 individuals, versus 578 in 51,765 non-SLD participants (0.74% vs. 1.12%). In this cohort, MASLD revealed an association with a greater risk of bladder cancer (aHR, 1.11; 95% CI, 1.01-1.21; P = 0.027), whereas MetALD showed a decreased risk (aHR, 0.67; 95% CI, 0.59-0.76; P < 0.001). The risk was more pronounced in individuals aged < 75 years and in those who engaged in moderate-to-vigorous physical activity. MASLD was associated with an increased risk of bladder cancer, and this association remained significant among never smokers after excluding cases within 3 years.

items.title: Inhibition of p38γ attenuates liver fibrosis progression by alleviating metabolic reprogramming.
items.abstract: Liver fibrosis, a consequence of chronic liver disease, commonly advances to cirrhosis and HCC without intervention. P38γ, a member of the four p38 mitogen-activated protein kinases (p38 MAPKs) isoforms, was involved in inflammation across several diseases, yet its impact on the activation of hepatic stellate cells (HSCs) during liver fibrosis remains elusive. Here, we demonstrated that the expression of p38γ was notably higher in fibrotic livers of humans and mice as well as activated LX-2 cells. P38γ knockout could significantly decrease the severity of liver fibrosis, as demonstrated by the attenuated proportion of activated HSCs in the liver and epithelial-mesenchymal transformation and immune cell infiltration. Knockdown of p38γ could block proliferation and phenotypic transformation of activated HSCs in TGF-β1-induced LX-2 cells. Interestingly, knockdown of p38γ could reduce glycolytic flux and TCA cycle, accumulation of glycolytic intermediates and PPP metabolites and enhanced PPP cycling. However, metabolomic analysis results showed that the levels of metabolites were decreased in cultured LX-2 cells after lentivirus-p38γ treatment. Mechanistically, p38γ bound directly to the pyruvate kinase M2 (PKM2) through its kinase domain, and facilitated the phosphorylation and nuclear movement of PKM2, along with suppressed PKM2 ubiquitination to enhance PKM2-mediated glycolysis, resulting in intracellular lactate accumulation. Elevated lactate levels enhance histone lactylation marks, thereby promoting HSCs phenotypic transformation. Activating PKM2 pharmacologically with DASA-58 partially reversed the glycolysis and activation of HSCs mediated by p38γ. In the absence of available p38γ inhibitors, we conducted high-throughput virtual screening and discovered Crocin I as a new p38γ inhibitor. Therapeutic administration of Crocin I improved liver fibrosis pathologies in mice with optimal safety. An exploratory clinical observation in ten patients suggested a trend toward reduced liver fibrosis after XHHZGP treatment. In conclusion, p38γ promotes the progression of liver fibrosis by inducing phenotypic transformation of activated HSCs based on the intracellular PKM2 reprogramming function of activated HSCs.

items.title: Identification of MRP2 and BCRP as the primary efflux transporters of 20-HETE glucuronide.
items.abstract: Although 20-hydroxyeicosatetraenoic acid (20-HETE) plays critical roles in the regulation of blood pressure and carcinogenesis, the transport mechanisms responsible for its cellular elimination remain largely unknown. This study aimed to identify the transporters responsible for the efflux of 20-HETE glucuronide. The mRNA and protein expression of efflux transporters, including multidrug resistance-associated proteins 1-5 (MRP1-​5), breast cancer resistance protein (BCRP), and multidrug resistance protein 1 (MDR1), were confirmed by reverse transcription PCR (RT-PCR), quantitative real-time PCR (qRT-PCR), and Western blot in HepG2 cells prior to functional studies of 20-HETE glucuronide transport. Treatment with MK571 (a pan-MRP inhibitor) and Ko143 (a selective BCRP inhibitor) concentration-dependently reduced the efflux of 20-HETE glucuronide from HepG2 cells by 69-90% (p < 0.001) and 58-63% (p < 0.01), respectively. Consistent with these findings, siRNA-mediated knockdown of MRP2 and BCRP significantly reduced the efflux of 20-HETE glucuronide from HepG2 cells by 47% (p < 0.05) and 32% (p < 0.05), respectively. Similar inhibitory effects were observed in Huh-7 cells, another human liver cell line, further confirming the role of these transporters in the efflux of 20-HETE glucuronide. Molecular docking analysis further revealed favorable binding interactions between 20-HETE glucuronide and both MRP2 and BCRP, providing additional support for their roles as the primary efflux transporters of 20-HETE glucuronide. In summary, the present study demonstrates that MRP2 and BCRP are the major transporters responsible for the efflux of 20-HETE glucuronide, providing new insights into the disposition of 20-HETE in humans.
